Article Title: Vande Mataram row: Congress hits out at Shah for demanding apology
Article Text: NEW DELHi: Attacking home minister Amit Shah for demanding an apology over the Vande Mataram row, Congress claimed the minister had insulted Bhimrao Ambedkar's memory in Rajya Sabha and that he owes allegiance to an organisation that did not unfurl the tricolour at its headquarters till 2002 - in what were allusions to Shah's controversial comments in the Upper house in Dec 2024 and to the RSS.AICC spokesperson Jairam Ramesh alleged, "A man who insulted Ambedkar on the floor of the Rajya Sabha on December 17, 2024. A man who belongs to an ideology that did not see it fit to unfurl the tiranga at its headquarters till January 2002. A man who orchestrated the Delhi Police's brutalities on peacefully protesting youth. Such a man is now demanding an apology from the Congress to divert attention away from the real issues of the day and away from colossal failures of his and his Sahib's. " TNN
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah has demanded an apology over the Vande Mataram row. Congress claimed the minister had insulted Bhimrao Ambedkar's memory in Rajya Sabha and that he owes allegiance to an organisation that did not unfurl the tricolour at its headquarters till 2002.

Article Title: Punjab Congress faces fresh rift as Randhawa challenges Warring's 'one family, one ticket' rule

NEW DELHI: Fresh differences emerged in the Punjab Congress on Sunday after MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa challenged state unit chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring's 'one family, one ticket' stance ahead of upcoming assembly elections.Speaking at an event attended by former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, Randhawa said families could get up to four tickets if their members were capable of winning."Some say I will not give two tickets (to a family). But those (in a family) who have the capability to win will not only get two but four tickets and ensure Congress' victory," Randhawa said.Randhawa also stressed that the Congress could not return to power by ignoring its workers."We have nurtured the Congress with our blood and sweat. If the Congress is standing strong in the state today, it is because of the contribution of every worker, not any one individual," he said.His remarks are being seen as a counter to Warring, who has advocated the 'one family, one ticket' policy.Warring had said that only one member of a family would get a ticket to contest the elections."Big leaders say I will contest from here and my son will contest from there.If Raja Warring stays, one family will get only one ticket, not two. Rahul Gandhi will give tickets, and I will only recommend," Warring had said.On Saturday, Warring also shared an old video of Rahul Gandhi on Facebook in which the former Congress president said, "One person per family should get a ticket.""I will always follow my leader and stand by him," Warring said.Meanwhile, BJP leader and former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu took a dig at the Congress over the issue, saying the party's high command itself does not follow the one-family-one-ticket policy.Bittu claimed that the Gandhi family had not followed the Congress' 2022 Udaipur declaration of 'one family, one ticket'."Is this a new thing? Sonia Gandhi is a Rajya Sabha member, while her children Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi are Lok Sabha members. What Randhawa Saab has said is completely right. When three members of the Gandhi family can sit in Parliament, why cannot a family get four tickets?" Bittu asked.The Punjab Congress has been grappling with factionalism despite repeated assertions by the party leadership that efforts are under way to strengthen organisational unity ahead of next year's Assembly elections.On July 1, when the Congress leadership decided to retain Warring as Punjab Congress chief and appoint Channi as chairman of its campaign committee.A section of leaders led by Channi had opposed Warring's continuation as state unit chief and sought his removal.Channi's supporters want him to be projected as the party's chief ministerial face ahead of the assembly polls.
Article Summary: Punjab Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa challenges state unit chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring's 'one family, one ticket' stance ahead of upcoming assembly elections. He said families could get up to four tickets if their members were capable of winning. Warring had said that only one member of a family would get a ticket to contest the elections.

Article Title: ‘Entire Bengal fuming’: Suvendu Adhikari slams Congress' Sonia Gandhi over I-Day Vande Mataram row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday slammed Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi over the controversy surrounding the recitation of Vande Mataram at the Congress headquarters on Independence Day , saying the 'Entire Bengal fuming, Congress must apologise'.Adhikari also accused the Congress of indulging in "appeasement politics"."It's appeasement politics, Cong trying to satisfy particular vote bank," he said while further adding that it's an insult to nationalism, and Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.The row erupted after visuals from the August 15 event showed senior Congress leaders speaking among themselves while Vande Mataram was being recited.BJP leaders has lodged a formal complaint against at the Urwa Police Station in Karnataka.The Congress has rejected the charge and said there was no attempt to stop the rendition.Maintaining that the allegations are baseless, the party said there was no attempt to stop the full version of Vande Mataram and that Sonia Gandhi was only trying to ensure proper arrangements at the event, including asking for a chair for Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, who had been standing.In a first for Independence Day celebrations, Vande Mataram, with all six stanzas, was rendered at the Red Fort complex on August 15, followed by the national anthem.
Article Summary: The row erupted after visuals from the August 15 event showed senior Congress leaders speaking among themselves while Vande Mataram was being recited. BJP leaders has lodged a formal complaint against at the Urwa Police Station in Karnataka. The Congress has rejected the charge and said there was no attempt to stop the rendition.

Article Title: 'Who is health minister saluting?' RJD mocks Nishant Kumar over flag-hoisting gesture - video
Article Text:
RJD targets Nishant Kumar over flag-hoisting video, asks ‘who is he saluting?’

The Rashtriya Janata Dal on Sunday targeted Bihar health minister Nishant Kumar by sharing a video of him hoisting the Tricolour on Independence Day. The Lalu Yadav-led party mocked former chief minister Nitish Kumar ’s son over his gesture shortly after the flag-hoisting.Posting the video on its official account, the RJD asked, “Who is the health minister saluting?”Taking its attack further, the main opposition party in Bihar said, “And to whom is he turning his back?”JD(U) leader Nishant Kumar, the son of Bihar’s longest-serving chief minister, has repeatedly come under the opposition’s scrutiny over his gestures on several occasions.Nishant Kumar was inducted into the state Cabinet soon after Samrat Choudhary became chief minister, replacing Nitish Kumar. Nitish subsequently became a Rajya Sabha member, marking the end of the Lalu-Nitish era in Bihar.
Article Summary: The Lalu Yadav-led party mocked former chief minister Nitish Kumar ’s son over his gesture shortly after the flag-hoisting. Nishant Kumar was inducted into the state Cabinet soon after Samrat Choudhary became chief minister.

Article Title: Prithviraj Chavan’s ‘Munde joining Congress’ claim refuted by Pankaja, Raut Weighs In
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A claim by former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan — that late BJP politician Gopinath Munde was planning to join Congress in 2011 — has triggered a political controversy, with BJP minister and Gopinath Munde's daughter Pankaja Munde dismissing the claim and Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut entering the debate.Speaking in Satara on Saturday, Chavan had said discussions to induct Munde into Congress had progressed significantly during his tenure as chief minister.“We had decided to bring her (Pankaja’s) father into Congress when I was chief minister and had obtained Sonia Gandhi 's approval too. Munde wanted a ministerial post as he would have had to resign and contest again, and feared BJP politicians from Nagpur would work against him,” Chavan said.Chavan claimed Munde, then a senior BJP functionary, was deeply unhappy within the saffron party and had held secret meetings with Congress office-bearers. “He came to meet me secretly in Delhi. Instead of staying at Maharashtra Sadan, I stayed in a private hotel. We held confidential meetings with Ahmed Patel. Munde was deeply unhappy at the time,” Chavan said.The former chief minister said the move ultimately did not materialise because the then prime minister, Dr Manmohan Singh , opposed the induction of a neta directly from the opposition.Chavan described assuring Munde of a ministerial position without first consulting Singh as the “biggest mistake” of his political career.Pankaja Munde, however, rejected claims that her father intended to leave BJP. “My father was born in a lotus, and rested in a lotus. Now that he is no longer alive, there is no point in engaging in such political discussions,” she told reporters in Beed on Saturday.Pankaja, however, said Chavan's remarks were not intended to disrespect her father and urged people not to misinterpret his statement.Meanwhile, Sanjay Raut said on Sunday that Munde might have avoided the circumstances he faced within BJP had he joined Congress. Raut also praised Singh for opposing such defections. “Manmohan Singh was against politicians switching parties in such a manner. Sharad Pawar too had offered a similar suggestion. Munde was being severely harassed by BJP. He was constantly subjected to mental trauma and insults,” Raut said.Gopinath Munde, a former deputy chief minister of Maharashtra and Union rural development minister, died in a road accident in New Delhi on June 3, 2014.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra chief minister Prithviraj Chavan claims Gopinath Munde was planning to join Congress in 2011. Chavan said discussions to induct Munde into Congress had progressed significantly during his tenure as chief minister. Munde wanted a ministerial post as he would have had to resign and contest again, he said.

Article Title: HC quashes FIR in leopard skin case, allows fresh proceedings
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed a 2022 FIR against two men allegedly found carrying leopard and other wildlife skins, ruling that the police head constable who lodged the complaint was not authorised to do so under section 55 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.Justice Abhay J Mantri, however, granted liberty to the competent authorities specified under section 55 to rectify the procedural defects and initiate fresh proceedings against the accused in accordance with the law.The FIR was registered against Bajirao Shripati Yadav and Bhramadev Shashikant Patil, both residents of Ajara tehsil, under sections 9, 39, 40, 43, 44 and 51 of the Act.The high court accepted the defence’s contention that section 55 bars courts from taking cognisance of offences under the Act unless a complaint is filed by an authorised official, such as the Director of Wildlife Preservation, the Chief Wildlife Warden or an officer specifically empowered for the purpose.The court relied on the Bombay high court’s ruling in Mannu Kaduba Gavane vs. State of Maharashtra (2016) and the Supreme Court’s decision in Elvish Yadav vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2026). It held that the special procedure prescribed under section 55 takes precedence over general criminal procedure and must be strictly followed.According to the case, Sambhaji Bhosale, head constable with Ispurli police station in Kolhapur’s Karvir tehsil, received information through an assistant police inspector that two men were allegedly planning to sell a leopard skin on Kolhapur-Gargoti Road near Dindnerli Phata.Bhosale led a police team that laid a trap and intercepted the suspects. A search allegedly led to the recovery of a leopard skin and the skins of other wild animals, following which the FIR was registered.“Nothing has been produced on record to indicate that Bhosale had authority to make a complaint as mandated in section 55 of the Act,” justice Mantri said in the order passed on Friday.The court observed that when a law prescribes a special procedural mechanism, it must be followed to the exclusion of general statutory provisions.
Article Summary: The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed a 2022 FIR against two men allegedly found carrying leopard and other wildlife skins. The court ruled that the police head constable who lodged the complaint was not authorised to do so under section 55 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.

Article Title: Sweeper dies after being run over by ST bus at workshop
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





A 55-year-old sweeper was killed after being run over by a state transport bus while climbing out of a vehicle inspection pit at the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation’s maintenance workshop near Kolhapur Central Bus Stand on Saturday morning.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Annappa Chavan, was a resident of Bhadole village and had been working as a sweeper at the workshop for several years.According to preliminary information, Chavan arrived at the workshop on Saturday morning and began cleaning the inspection pit. After coming out, he reportedly re-entered the pit to retrieve an item he had left behind. Around the same time, an ST bus entered the workshop. Assuming that no one was inside the pit, the driver proceeded forward. However, after hearing a loud thud, he stopped the bus.“Chavan had injuries on his head and legs. He was rushed to the CPR Hospital where he died. We have registered the offence against the driver under section 106 of BNS. The deceased’s son has filed a complaint. The driver is yet to be arrested,” Sagar Gunvare, sub-inspector of Shahupuri Police Station, said.
Article Summary: A 55-year-old sweeper was killed after being run over by a state transport bus in Kolhapur. Pandurang Annappa Chavan was climbing out of a vehicle inspection pit at the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation’s maintenance workshop. The deceased had been working at the workshop for several years.

Article Title: Ambernath BJP-MNS clash: Case registered against 2 BJP corporators, five others
Article Text:
A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash.





AMBERNATH: The political clash between BJP and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers in Ambernath has taken a fresh turn, with Shivaji Nagar police registering a fresh case against seven people, including two BJP corporators, on the complaint of an MNS worker who was injured in the incident.The latest case was registered on Sunday on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash. Police have booked BJP corporators Abhijit Karanjule and Pawan Walekar along with five others under sections 118(1), 115(2), 189(2), 190, 191(2) and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The development comes days after police arrested Shirke and some of his associates for allegedly assaulting BJP office-bearer Laxmi Narayan Chauhan at his office in Vadavali.A subsequent clash between BJP and MNS workers at Shivaji Nagar police station further escalated tensions.MNS leaders had alleged that police took one-sided action by arresting their office-bearers while failing to act against BJP workers allegedly involved in the assault on Shirke. MNS leader Avinash Jadhav had demanded action against those responsible.Following the demand, MNS district president Bandu Deshmukh had announced a protest on Sunday against what the party termed one-sided police action. However, after police registered an FIR against BJP workers, MNS withdrew its protest.
Article Summary: A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash. The latest case was registered on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash.

Article Title: 21 stray dogs, 2 cats poisoned in Nashik village, 2 booked
Article Text:
Nashik

:





In a case of animal cruelty, the Deola police have booked two residents of Lohoner village in Nashik district for allegedly poisoning 21 stray dogs and two cats earlier this week.The accused have been identified as Ramesh Ahire and Mukesh, alias Papa Pardeshi. An FIR was registered on Aug 14 under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and the Maharashtra Police Act.According to the police, information was received on the morning of Aug 13 about the deaths of several stray animals near the Balaji temple and the Maharashtra Bank areas of Lohoner village. Inspector Sarthak Nehete, assistant Inspector Vinay Devre and constable Suresh Ramesh Korade visited the spot.During the investigation, the police found that the accused had allegedly purchased raw chicken from a local butcher around 7.30pm on Aug 12 and later bought toxic pesticides from a nearby shop. The pesticide was allegedly mixed with the chicken and fed to stray dogs and cats at different locations in the village.On the morning of Aug 13, sanitation worker Kantilal Salunkhe found 20 dogs and two cats dead. Unaware of police procedures, he collected the carcasses and buried them in a pit behind the village Amrutdham ground using a JCB machine.While inspecting the area, the police reportedly saw another dog foaming at the mouth and writhing in pain before collapsing. The animal was immediately taken to the Deola veterinary hospital for postmortem and sample collection.Following the postmortem findings and verification of the burial site, constable Korade lodged the complaint against the two accused. The police said the accused deliberately laced chicken pieces with poison and fed them to the animals. Inspector Sarthak Nehete is conducting further investigation.
Article Summary: The Deola police have booked two residents of Lohoner village in Nashik district for allegedly poisoning 21 stray dogs and two cats. The accused have been identified as Ramesh Ahire and Mukesh, alias Papa Pardeshi. The police said the accused deliberately laced chicken pieces with poison and fed them to the animals.

Article Title: Coimbatore district police arrest man for derogatory posts about Lord Murugan
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Periyanaickenpalayam police in Coimbatore district arrested a man on charges of posting derogatory comments about Hindu deity Lord Murugan on social media.Police arrested Michael of Rakkipalayam based on a complaint filed by M Shankar, who is the Narasimhanaickenpalayam union general secretary of Hindu Munnani. He alleged that Michael, through posts on Instagram and Facebook, used offensive words and made disparaging remarks targeting Lord Murugan that could disturb public peace and incite religious tension.Based on the complaint, police registered a case and arrested Michael, who is a TVK supporter.Cases were registered against Michael in several districts on the same issue, police sources said. Officials from the respective district police units have contacted the Coimbatore district police to coordinate efforts to arrest him.
Article Summary: Police arrested Michael of Rakkipalayam based on a complaint filed by M Shankar, who is the Narasimhanaickenpalayam union general secretary of Hindu Munnani. He alleged that Michael used offensive words and made disparaging remarks targeting Lord Murugan.

Article Title: Former TVK candidate Arun Kumar joins AIADMK
Article Text:
Salem





: Former TVK candidate M Arun Kumar on Saturday joined AIADMK after meeting party general secretary and former chief minister Edappadi K Palaniswami at the latter’s residence here.Arun Kumar, who had earlier served as the AIADMK union councillor in Ayothiapattinam, later joined TVK. He was initially announced as the TVK candidate in the Edappadi assembly constituency. His nomination was rejected after election officials found that the proposers listed in his papers could not be verified. The substitute candidate’s papers were also rejected on similar grounds, leaving TVK without a contender against Palaniswami in the constituency.By joining the AIADMK, Arun Kumar shifted political loyalties, strengthening the party’s grassroots presence in Salem district.(Photos: TOI)
Article Summary: Arun Kumar had earlier served as the AIADMK union councillor in Ayothiapattinam. He was initially announced as the TVK candidate in the Edappadi assembly constituency. His nomination was rejected after election officials found that the proposers listed in his papers could not be verified.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.
